goal:
H26-3: improve the existing three-game clip-to-practice flow with accurate game-specific practice steps and controls, and deterministic hosted runtime/health metadata. Preserve existing clip upload/trim/linkage, relay/replay/proof behavior, original practice environments and supplied FaZe toolkit fonts/logos. Use https://hackuta26.onrender.com/ as the current hosted browser baseline; candidate changes are tested locally until deployment is separately authorized.

Runtime interface: server/runtime-config.ts exports resolveRuntimeConfig(env: Record<string,string|undefined>) -> {host:string,port:number,commit:string|null}. Trim HOST; nonblank explicit HOST wins; otherwise exactly RENDER='true' defaults to 0.0.0.0, local defaults to 127.0.0.1. Trim PORT; unset/blank uses 5173; otherwise ASCII digits only, integer 0..65535, invalid throws a clear startup error without exposing the supplied value. Trim 40-hex RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, accept either case and normalize lowercase; invalid/unset is null. Bootstrap consumes this result. Health preserves ok:true/service:'run-it-back' and always includes commit, with no arbitrary environment details.

Guide interface: packages/challenges/practice-guide.ts exports practiceGuide(config: ChallengeConfig) -> {title:string,steps:string[],controls:string[]}, for valid configs only. Seven presets: jump, spin180, spin360, ramp-shot, wall-edit, precision, dash-peek. Controls reflect real WASD, mouse/arrow/Q/E aiming/turning, C aim-down-sights, F fire, R retry; Space only in non-tactical modes, B for buildyard, G only for wall-edit, X only for dash-peek. Align assist absent for spin presets. Describe actual ramp takeoff, wall opening/jump/fire, net airborne spin, grounded stationary precision, and covered left-crate dash followed by stop/fire. Tactical wording is turn, not spin. Use replay?.config ?? config for guide/objective when replaying. No automatic detection/reconstruction/anti-cheat or fabricated completion claims. Keep typography Source/Anton and supplied logos only.

Acceptance: independent regression tests and existing suite pass; production build passes; independent exact-SHA review; actual candidate browser checks for representative presets/config switching and separate hosted-baseline observations. No Render settings change, integration/main merge or deployment is included in worker work.

# Hackuta26 five-role team

Codex 1 coordinates ideas, architecture, roadmap, assignments, review disposition and final decisions. Human instructions take precedence.

- Codex 1: docs/, shared/, root configuration and integration.
- Codex 2: server/ and packages/social/ except tests; non-UI application and persistence.
- Codex 3: src/, packages/challenges/ and packages/gameplay/ except tests; all frontend.
- Claude 1: independent plan and actual diff review, no author edits.
- Claude 2: tests/ and all *.test.ts; independent edge cases and regressions.

Cycle: plan, review plan, propose implementation, coordinator application, independent tests, actual checks, review changes, owner revisions, integration. Keep owned paths separate. Shared interface and dependency changes go through Codex 1. Record handoffs in docs/team/.

Permanent role folders are team/roles/ROLE/; read team/roles/README.md for ownership and isolation rules. Use your own complete worktree at ../agent-worktrees/ROLE/ and agents/ROLE branch as the starting point. Never edit or switch branches in another role's working folder. Each role records new handoffs in its own team/roles/ROLE/ folder; docs/team/ retains historical evidence. These folders and branch rules coordinate writes; they are not filesystem access controls.

The human resumed bounded hackathon work under Codex 1 coordination. Read team/state.json, docs/H26-3-PLAN.md and remote automation/control.json for the current goal and status. Do not restart the old dispatcher. Codex 3 must verify its previously blocked coding-file access before implementation. No task assignment authorizes a main/integration merge or deployment.

The human now authorizes building/publishing the cross-computer relay described in docs/AUTOMATION.md. Codex 1 controls automation/queue; workers follow bounded assignments through scripts/relay.mjs. Setup does not resume features. Only a real explicit human resume recorded in remote control humanResume may supersede the historical paused text for that approved goal. The runner may commit/publish its own validated task branches as part of that goal; no main/integration merge or deployment is implied. Do not fabricate approval text or start a second worker for an active role.

The original local message service dispatches read-only proposals, not edits or commands. Desktop applied reviewed proposals and executed checks; do not claim independent execution. For the four-computer workflow use separate clones/worktrees and the optional running relay workers, per-role tasks, topic branches and PR handoffs. GitHub alone does not dispatch agents; scripts/relay.mjs does so only while its local processes run. Keep account files, service credentials, logs and player data outside Git. Respect account limits.

User authorized the local build, repository creation, and now publishing the reviewed build and multi-computer setup to Kx007-del/hackuta26 so the five roles can work through GitHub. This authorizes the setup upload on build/five-agent-h26, not future unrestricted pushes. Main merges and deployment still require explicit approval. Keep old hackuta and faze-run-it-back repositories unchanged.

Read docs/ROADMAP.md and shared/contracts.ts. Current H26-2 scope: clip upload/preview/trim, original Rooftop/Buildyard/Courtyard environments, mode-specific jump/spin/build/edit/stationary/dash proof, harder remixes, two-person relay and sequential replays. Read docs/H26-2-PLAN.md. Only toolkit Source/Anton fonts and supplied FaZe logos; preserve provenance. No automatic video reconstruction or anti-cheat claims. Balance substantive work across all three Codex and two Claude profiles; both Claude profiles are pinned to claude-opus-5-5.

# Permanent agent folders and ownership

Confirmed against the original human assignment in “Set up four-agent coding workflow”, chat 01a1d97c-5635-7271-94fe-19bd246f3473, role-assignment turn 01a1d99e-dcbf-7701-a79e-41cd1d21e54f. Codex 1 was assigned ideas, thinking, plans and roadmap; Codex 2 execution; Codex 3 UI/frontend; Claude 1 review/improvements/errors; Claude 2 tests/edge cases. Later instructions made Codex 1 coordinator with final say among agents, required balanced substantive effort, and pinned both Claude profiles to Opus 5.5. Human authority takes precedence.

| Role folder | Local full working copy, relative to the project folder | Git branch | Device |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| codex-1/ | agent-worktrees/codex-1/ | agents/codex-1 | Windows 1 |
| codex-2/ | agent-worktrees/codex-2/ | agents/codex-2 | Mac |
| codex-3/ | agent-worktrees/codex-3/ | agents/codex-3 | Windows 3 |
| claude-1/ | agent-worktrees/claude-1/ | agents/claude-1 | Windows 1 |
| claude-2/ | agent-worktrees/claude-2/ | agents/claude-2 | Windows 2 |

Each role writes its task notes/handoffs only in its own tracked role folder. Codex 1 may maintain this index. The application source is not duplicated into these tracked folders; each separate local worktree already contains the whole application on an independent branch. The GitHub role branches are starting points, not proof of live signed-in agent sessions.

Ownership:
- Codex 1: docs/, shared/, root configuration, coordination and integration. Route shared contracts/dependencies here.
- Codex 2: server/ and packages/social/, excluding all test files.
- Codex 3: src/, packages/challenges/ and packages/gameplay/, excluding all test files.
- Claude 1: independent plan and exact-head diff review; write findings in its own role folder or GitHub, never patch an author's branch.
- Claude 2: tests/ and all *.test.ts, plus its own role folder. Tests inside an implementation package belong to Claude 2, not that package's implementation owner.

Before editing, claim a bounded GitHub task with base SHA and owned paths. Start a work/ROLE/TASK branch in your own worktree. Never switch branches or run edits in another role's folder. Never reset, clean, force-push, stash or overwrite another role's work. If an owned-path change needs another owner, ask Codex 1 to record a temporary assignment first. Full worktree visibility is needed for reading and testing; these are coordination rules, not filesystem permission boundaries.

Record every handoff with task, role, base/head SHA, files, checks actually run, findings and next owner. Claude 2 tests the actual implementation commit; Claude 1 reviews the actual final diff. Codex 1 integrates after review/checks and required human approval. Git does not automatically merge role branches or wake agents; the optional running relay in docs/AUTOMATION.md dispatches tasks through GitHub under Codex 1's control.

Feature development remains paused. Only setup and connection checks may run until the human resumes. Follow team/state.json and docs/MULTI-COMPUTER.md. Keep credentials, local databases, uploads, dependencies and generated build output out of Git; package-lock.json and build commands reproduce the build.

# H26-3 — hosted testing and game-specific practice guidance

The human resumed project work and requested continuous coordination of the five assigned accounts. The shared browser test target is https://hackuta26.onrender.com/. GitHub remains the source of truth. No main/integration merge or hosting change is implied by a worker task.

Baseline: H26-2 is implemented with 49 passing tests and a production build. On the hosted site the homepage and /api/health return 200; actual browser navigation opens the clip workbench and tactical arena. The public health response currently has only ok/service, so the exact deployed commit cannot be identified from it. The served main bundle filenames match the last locally verified build; this is not proof of an exact Git SHA. The connected Render account is different from the hosting account, so deploy branch/automatic deploy/persistent storage settings remain unverified.

## Bounded outcome

Make the existing three-game clip-to-practice flow easier to understand and the hosted build easier to identify/test. Preserve clip upload/trim, exact arena/config linkage, replay/relay proof rules, and toolkit-only fonts/logos. These remain original browser practice arenas, not official game engines or copied maps. No new video-AI claims, external game assets, accounts, paid services or storage migrations.

## Five-role deliverables

1. Codex 1: plan, frozen interfaces, task allocation, exact-SHA integration, hosted baseline/browser evidence and final disposition. Maintain substantive balance, not message counts.
2. Claude 1: first independently review this plan and actual relevant files. After changes, review exact tested diffs, misleading claims, brand provenance and error cases. Review-only, Opus 5.5.
3. Codex 2 (Mac): implement server/runtime-config.ts exporting resolveRuntimeConfig(env: Record<string, string | undefined>) returning {host: string, port: number, commit: string | null}. Preserve local host 127.0.0.1 and default port 5173. Use 0.0.0.0 by default only when RENDER === 'true'; explicit nonblank HOST wins. PORT must be an integer from 0 through 65535 (0 supports ephemeral local tests); blank/unset uses 5173, invalid values fail clearly. commit is a validated 40-hex-character RENDER_GIT_COMMIT or null; no other environment information is returned. Bootstrap uses this config, and GET /api/health preserves {ok:true, service:'run-it-back'} plus commit. Own server/ only for this task, excluding tests. Do not change deployed Render settings or persistence.
4. Codex 3 (Windows 3): after its file-access preflight succeeds, add a compact, accessible, config-driven practice guide for all seven presets. Own src/ and packages/challenges/ plus relevant non-test gameplay UI. Expose packages/challenges/practice-guide.ts with practiceGuide(config: ChallengeConfig): {title: string, steps: string[], controls: string[]} for independent tests. Show concrete ordered actions for jump, spin180/360, ramp-shot, wall-edit, precision and dash-peek; controls must match real implemented keys (Space, Q/E, B/G, X, F/R), and show turn rather than spin wording for tactical play. Reflect the selected config on switching/remix/invitation. Describe reference clips honestly as player-guided; do not fabricate live completion indicators. Do not change physics/proof contracts, unrelated graphics or font/logo sources. Polish existing per-game control hints to expose the correct actions, without creating a second input system.
5. Claude 2 (Windows 2): independent contract-driven tests for runtime host/port/commit handling and the seven preset guides, plus existing regression suite and brand guards. Work from actual published implementation SHAs, tests/ and *.test.ts only. Add meaningful assertions for mode-specific controls and malformed config/runtime input where contracted; do not merely snapshot the implementation. Report actual commands/results. Opus 5.5. Browser checks require actual browser tools; otherwise explicitly hand them to desktop Codex 1.

Codex 2 and Codex 3 are parallel implementations after plan review. Shared interfaces above belong to Codex 1. Claude 2 tests a combined integration SHA or explicit individual implementation SHAs; Claude 1 reviews the final tested combined SHA. Owners fix their findings; Codex 1 integrates only reviewed/tested work on a separate branch. No agent edits another role's working tree.

## Access and publication gates

Coordination update: Codex 3's local preflight confirmed a real host-policy rejection before PowerShell starts; keep its worker in read-only proposal mode. Codex 3 still authors frontend code from supplied source packets; desktop Codex 1 applies reviewed proposals in its authorized workspace and records authorship versus execution explicitly. This preserves the original coordinator-mediated workflow without weakening the remote policy. Its tool permissions are not claimed fixed. The Mac's first turn was instead blocked by a coordinator-only instruction leaking into its shared goal; no Mac permission failure or source change was established. Product requirements and coordinator operating notes must be separate before the corrected cycle.

Claude 1's plan corrections are frozen: practiceGuide accepts valid ChallengeConfig only; use replay?.config ?? config for guides and objective distance. Every mode includes actual WASD/aim/C/F/R controls; Space is excluded for tactical, G is wall-edit-only, X is dash-peek-only, and ALIGN is absent for spin presets. Steps must describe real ramp takeoff, wall opening and cover/dash/settle requirements. Trim HOST/PORT; blank PORT defaults, otherwise ASCII digits only 0..65535. Trim valid case-insensitive 40-hex commit and normalize lowercase; invalid gives null. These update the initial wording above.

Codex 3 previously had a real execution-policy rejection reading project files. Its later successful transport check did not prove coding access. Do not assign implementation to it until the local worker's read/owned-folder-write capability is verified. Diagnose policy normally; never disable security controls or bypass permissions. If backend or coordinator tooling is blocked too, report the exact blocker without claiming execution.

The resumed user instruction authorizes bounded work and publication of unique task branches. Render's deployment source/settings must be confirmed before pushing an integration branch that might auto-deploy. Do not trigger a deployment or change hosting resources while that information is missing. Use the public Render site for current-build read-only/browser QA, and locally test candidate changes before any separately authorized deploy. Uploaded QA data must be clearly synthetic/disposable; do not touch existing player records.

## Acceptance

- Runtime config and health commit identity are deterministic and expose no credentials or arbitrary environment values.
- Every preset has correct, readable steps and controls; switching games/presets updates the guide; labels describe original practice mechanics honestly.
- Existing relay, clip, proof and brand behavior remains intact; independent new tests and existing tests pass; production build passes.
- Independent exact-diff review is resolved. Actual local browser checks cover representative rooftop, build/edit and dash/settle guides, including config switching. Record the hosted baseline separately from candidate/local results.
- Report actual role responses, source SHAs, validation evidence and remaining access/deployment limits. No statement that the live URL contains new changes until its deployed revision is verified.

Official Render environment reference consulted: https://render.com/docs/environment-variables.md (RENDER, RENDER_GIT_COMMIT and PORT). No Render account settings were changed.
